declared.title: The effects of informal digital learning, intrinsic motivation, and grit on online learning effort regulation and English achievement
declared.foundIn: reports/choose-your-struggle/counter-evidence.md (card 20); OpenAlex search « Alshammari Alrashidi informal digital learning English intrinsic motivation grit Saudi » (2026-11-26)

population: 218 Saudi students of English as a foreign language at the University of Ha'il (56% men), one online questionnaire translated into Arabic

findings.text: Intrinsic motivation went with more self-reported regulation of effort in online learning; grit had no unique path to effort once the other predictors were in the model (its simple correlation with effort is positive, r = .57)

support.sentence: The results indicated that IDLE and intrinsic motivation had significant positive effects on OLER, while grit did not significantly influence OLER.

findings.text: English achievement went with grit; intrinsic motivation had no unique path to it once the other predictors were in the model (its simple correlation with achievement is positive, r = .34)

support.sentence: For English achievement, grit had a significant positive effect, while IDLE and intrinsic motivation had insignificant effects.

limits: one questionnaire at one time: the « effects » are paths of a structural model, not causes (the authors say so)
intrinsic motivation and reported effort correlate at r = .88, above the Fornell-Larcker bound: almost one measure taken twice, the same day, by the same person (acknowledged)
achievement: course grades and a standardized English proficiency test, converted to one scale (full text, PMC13128827)
one university, convenience sample, students learning English online; 56% men, 44% women
a Saudi sample (Ha'il), instruments translated into Arabic and back-translated, piloted on 30 students; no Egyptian sample
